research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10848 at 24 FR 8401 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 14, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 16, 1959 issue. The order amends Executive Order No. 10843 of October 9, 1959, which created a board of inquiry on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry.  Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 726 to 954 and 2439 to 2738 of the held text. The text layer places a Farmers Home Administration regulation (Title 6, Part 341) between the words amending 'the second sentence in the penultimate paragraph of Executive Order No. 10843' and their continuation. The dossier's two spans include that unrelated regulation text; the order's own text is the enacting words through the identification of the parent order, and the continuation through the replacement sentence and the signing block's date. Content: acting under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, it amends the second sentence of the penultimate paragraph of Executive Order No. 10843 to read that the Board shall report to the President on or before October 19, 1959. It is a one-time amendment of a report date and has no other command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10848 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads thTstell Tndust^6 ° rder N°' 10843 CreatÌng 8 b° ard ° f ÌnqUÌry t0 report on a labor dispute affecting and the garbled text layer reads the entry as ending with a reference to Executive Order No. 10843 creating a board of inquiry on a labor dispute affecting the steel industry; the identification rests on the number in the number column). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report date, as substituted, is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling of 2026-10-21, report deadline); no board report for Executive Order 10843 is held in the packet, so no functionally-spent date is recorded. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain no end date or termination clause; the packet's number search finds no held text citing this order; the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.
